newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME copper seen falling short of US$2,500 barrier.
newsitem.headline: LME copper seen falling short of US$2,500 barrier.

text.p: Copper prices on the London Metal Exchange (LME) are expected to drift lower later on Tuesday and any challenge of key overhead resistance for three month metal at the US$2,500 level is seen failing, traders said.
"I feel $2,500 is out of my target. We should be in for some consolidation," a dealer for a European metal trading firm said.

Another dealer said the topside for copper, which finished the kerb on the LME on Monday at $2,474 a tonne, "is very limited. At most, it would be $2,475 or even $2,485. I doubt it would go up to $2,500."
LME metal brokers Brandeis said in its daily review that copper had a "reasonable close on the charts" and had been able to rally in the past despite an overbought market.
"We see prices struggling to make new highs unless a correction is seen first," it said.
Brokers Macquarie said in its report the lack of follow through interest combined with the lending of the near month spreads capped prices on Monday.
Three month copper was being quoted by Far East dealers at 0230 GMT at $2,465/70 a tonne.
Traders said they had heard reports of some Chinese merchants offering copper, but the volumes involved were modest.
Talk was also circulating in the market that the Chinese were about to ship zinc to Singapore warehouses, dealers said.
"I understand the Chinese are checking zinc prices. I heard they were close to selling," one said.
"I haven't seen the Chinese coming into the zinc market here," a European metal dealer said.
The trade was also monitoring the start this week of talks in Japan, South Korea and Taiwan for third quarter aluminium supply contracts.
Suppliers are pushing for premiums in all three countries to be increased to a base of $90 a tonne CIF against $80-$85 in the second quarter of 1997.
"It's still very early in the contract talks. It will take some time before we see something," an aluminium dealer said.
Three month aluminium was seen by the trade at 0230 GMT at $1,654/58 a tonne, up from the kerb close on the LME of $1,648.
Copper and aluminium inventories were expected to fall when the LME stocks report comes out at 0800 GMT, dealers said.
